flags: 'Accent supervision' is not an established term in professional sound-for-picture, dubbing/localization, or audio-engineering literature. No standards body, manufacturer technical document, or recognized professional text (Yewdall, Holman, Rose; AVT/localization references) defines a role, process, or deliverable by this name. Its sense is ambiguous (dialect/accent coaching vs. localization QA vs. reading a musical accent) and it is not a transparent compound of a defined audio technique plus a source/section, so it cannot be authored to a professional standard. 'Braam' (also 'braaam'/'brami') is a real modern trailer and cinematic sound-design device — a massive, distorted, brass-like low-end impact popularized after Inception (2010) — but it is attested only in trade press, blogs, Wikipedia, and vendor sample-library listings, none of which are acceptable corroborating sources. No standards body, manufacturer technical document, or recognized professional post-production/sound-design text (Yewdall, Holman, Sonnenschein, Viers, Ament) defines it, and as a coined onomatopoeic name it is not a transparent technique-plus-source compound. fields.definition: In 3D and game audio, the reduction in a directional sound source's gain applied as the listener moves off the source's projection axis: full gain applies within the inner cone angle, gain is interpolated across the transition zone between the inner and outer cone angles, and the source drops to a set outer-cone gain factor beyond the outer cone angle.
fields.plain_english: A way to make a sound quieter when you are off to the side of what makes it. A sound source can aim like a flashlight beam. You hear it at full volume in the beam, and it fades as you step out of it.
fields.purpose_function: It models the directivity of real sources such as a speaking mouth, a horn, or a TV, so a 3D sound softens when the listener is off-axis, adding realism and useful spatial cues to an interactive scene.
fields.practical_application: A game-audio designer sets a source's inner cone angle, outer cone angle, and outer-cone gain in middleware or a game engine (Wwise, FMOD, Unreal, or OpenAL) so a directional emitter quiets down as the player moves out of its cone.
common_mistakes: Confusing cone attenuation with distance falloff; the cone sets level by the listener's angle to the source, while falloff sets level by distance.
Leaving the outer-cone gain at zero by accident, so the source goes fully silent the instant the listener steps outside the cone.
Setting the inner and outer cone angles equal, which removes the smooth transition zone and causes an abrupt level jump off-axis.
scenario_contexts: Making an NPC's voice quieter when the player walks around behind them.
Aiming a loudspeaker or television emitter in a level so it projects sound forward.
Tuning a directional machine or vent so it only reads loud when faced head-on.

sources: OpenAL 1.1 Specification and Reference (AL_CONE_INNER_ANGLE, AL_CONE_OUTER_ANGLE, AL_CONE_OUTER_GAIN)
Epic Games, Unreal Engine documentation: Sound Attenuation (Cone attenuation shape)
FMOD Engine documentation: 3D Sounds white paper

fields.definition: In interactive game audio, a game-sync value (a Wwise State, a switch, or an engine parameter) that flags the player as being in an exploration, non-combat context, used by the audio system to select or blend the ambience and adaptive-music layers appropriate to that state.
fields.plain_english: A setting that tells the game you are just exploring, not fighting. The game reads it and plays calmer background music. When the state changes, the music changes to match what you do.
fields.purpose_function: It lets the soundtrack respond to gameplay by tying a named game state to the right music and ambience, so the mood shifts automatically as the player moves between exploring and other situations such as combat.
fields.practical_application: A game-audio designer maps the game's exploration state to a State or parameter in middleware such as Wwise or FMOD, then routes it to a music switch container so exploration music plays and transitions out when combat begins.
common_mistakes: Thinking the parameter itself makes sound; it only reports the game state, and the audio system must be set up to react to it.
Forgetting to define musical transitions, so the switch from exploration to combat music cuts abruptly instead of blending.
Confusing a discrete state (a game context like exploration) with a continuous parameter such as distance or intensity.
scenario_contexts: Playing calm exploration music that swells into combat music when enemies appear.
Switching ambient beds as the player leaves a safe town and enters open wilderness.
Debugging why exploration music keeps playing after a fight has already started.

sources: Audiokinetic, Wwise documentation: Game Syncs (Switches and States) and Music Switch Container
Stevens & Raybould, The Game Audio Tutorial

After searching the professional film-sound and audio literature, no >=2 acceptable sources define 'finger tap' as a distinct term, and it is not a transparent technique-plus-source compound.
